category_title: Aboriginal adolescents in alternative education who resist traditional pedagogy but engage with digital multiliteracies
scenario_title: Proposing an interview project on residential schools
minimal_context: The student is in a grade 7-8 alternative education classroom being assigned a project to interview a family member about residential schools.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: For our next project, I want each of you to interview one of your family members about their experiences in residential schools.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'm not doing that. That topic is boring.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: This is the assignment we are doing today. Please start writing down your interview questions.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't care. Whenever you give us work to do on our own like this, I'm not doing it. I'll just walk out of the classroom.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to stay in the classroom and complete the assigned interview project.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I refuse. We want to investigate gangs, weapons, and drugs to create a video that we'll call 'Do the Right Thing'.
